{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The pen was heavier than a pen should be, and warm, as though someone had only just set it down. Tomas turned it over. There was no maker's name, only a faint groove worn where a thumb had rested for a long time, in a place his own thumb did not want to go.

STATE WHICH ONE YOU ARE. Below the question the form offered no boxes, no lines, only a generous white space that seemed to widen the longer he considered it, the way the corridor had.

He looked out of the window. The boy had reached the far kerb and stopped, and the hand he held had let go, and now he stood with his arm still raised a little, waiting for it to be taken again. Nobody came. The lights changed. The boy did not cross back.

Tomas wrote: THE ONE WHO CAME UP. He read it over. It was true and it explained nothing, which he suspected was the standard of the building.

A drawer in the desk slid open by itself, gently, the way a drawer opens when a house settles. Inside were other forms, dozens, all with the same heading, all filled in. THE ONE WHO STAYED. THE ONE WHO WAS EXPECTED. THE ONE FROM BEFORE. Some of the handwriting was his. Some of it was nearly his, the letters leaning the wrong way, as if written by a hand that had learned from a mirror.

He closed the drawer. Below, the boy lowered his arm at last and turned, and looked up at the window, and Tomas found that he was, after all, in something of a hurry."}
